title: Sequon import report (sequon/import-report/1)
description: Import report produced by Sequon adapters. Schemas are self-contained: this document does not $ref the record schema. This JSON Schema validates structure and value domains only. Cross-field invariants are not expressible in JSON Schema and are owned by Record::validate(): records[].length equals the record sequence length, records[].sequence_digest and records[].canonical_digest equal the recomputed sha256 values, and dropped/preserved entries referring to a record agree with the bytes actually skipped or kept. The report is an event document: it is never written back into a record.
$comment: Field order in a canonical document follows the declaration order of this schema's properties. Serialization rule for optional fields: nullable fields (description, molecule_type, feature.so_term, feature.name, diagnostic.position, diagnostic.record_index) are always present in a canonical document and are JSON null when unknown; non-nullable optional fields (dropped and preserved convenience fields) are omitted when unknown. Schema validation accepts the absence of both kinds so hand-authored documents remain valid. diagnostics are ordered deterministically; see docs/design/diagnostics.md for codes_version, severity semantics, the dropped.reason vocabulary and consumer handling of unknown codes.

schema.description: Contract identifier for this report version.

source_format.description: Format of the imported source. One report never mixes formats.

source_digest.description: sha256 of the exact source bytes that were imported.

source_bytes.description: Length of the source input in bytes.

export_version.description: SnapGene export version read from the container; null for formats that do not carry one.

codes_version.description: Version of the diagnostic code table this report was produced with (for example '2026-10-21/1'). The table is append-only; consumers use this value to interpret codes and must tolerate codes they do not know.

records.description: One entry per record returned by the import, in output order. A report for a rejected import is not produced; the typed error is returned instead.

diagnostics.description: Warnings and informational events, and error-severity entries for records that failed while the import still produced a usable report. Ordered deterministically by position then code.

dropped.description: Blocks or features that were skipped, with a fingerprint. Mutually exclusive with 'preserved' for the same range: bytes that are kept go to 'preserved', bytes that are only fingerprinted go to 'dropped'.

preserved.description: Raw source blocks kept verbatim (base64) because the canonical model cannot express them. The report never rewrites a record from these entries.

index.description: Zero-based position of the record in the import output. Diagnostics refer to it with record_index.

name.description: Record name as it appears in the canonical record.

length.description: Number of bases or residues. Record::validate() requires it to equal the record sequence length.

sequence_digest.description: Copy of the record's direction-sensitive sequence digest.

canonical_digest.description: Copy of the record's canonical digest; the permanent, rotation- and strand-invariant identity.

code.description: Diagnostic code from docs/design/diagnostics.md. Stable identifier; consumers switch on it and must not reject a report because a code is unknown.

severity.description: error: the record is unusable; warning: the record is usable but something was lost or reinterpreted; info: normal but worth recording.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Never contains sequence content or raw source bytes; positions and identifiers only.

position.description: Source position, or null when the event has no position. Always present in a canonical report; null means 'not applicable'.

record_index.description: Index of the affected record in records[], or null when the event is not tied to one record. Always present in a canonical report.

line.description: 1-based line number in the decoded source text.

column.description: 1-based column, present only when the adapter knows it (for example a malformed location or qualifier). Line-only positions omit it.

offset.description: 0-based byte offset in the source container.

packet_type.description: TLV packet type, when the position is inside a packet or the error concerns the packet header.

packet_index.description: 0-based index of the packet in the container's TLV sequence.

sourcePosition.description: Where in the source the event happened. A report carries positions of one format only, because it describes one import.

what.description: Adapter-defined kind of the skipped item, for example 'trace_container', 'unknown_packet', 'alignable_sequence', or 'feature'.

reason.description: Adapter-defined snake_case reason. When a diagnostic code explains the loss, reason equals that code (for example 'unsupported_location' is accompanied by GB_LOCATION_UNSUPPORTED); otherwise it is one of the reserved reasons defined in docs/design/diagnostics.md (for example 'size_limit').

record_index.description: Record the skipped item belongs to, when it belongs to one record.

packet_type.description: Convenience copy of the packet type for SnapGene items.

offset.description: Convenience copy of the 0-based byte offset of the skipped bytes.

length.description: Length of the skipped bytes, when known.

digest.description: sha256 of the skipped bytes, so the loss is auditable.

feature_key.description: GenBank feature key of a skipped feature (present only when 'what' is a feature).

location_text.description: Source location text of a skipped feature, kept verbatim so the loss can be reproduced (present only when 'what' is a feature).

what.description: Adapter-defined kind of the kept block, for example 'unknown_packet', 'history', or 'alignable_sequence'.

encoding.description: Payload encoding. v1 only defines base64.

data.description: The raw bytes of the block, base64-encoded. Capped by the configured limits; oversized blocks are fingerprinted into 'dropped' instead.

packet_type.description: Convenience copy of the packet type for SnapGene blocks.

offset.description: Convenience copy of the 0-based byte offset of the kept bytes.

length.description: Length of the kept bytes before base64 encoding.

digest.description: sha256 of the kept bytes, so a preserved block can be verified.

record_index.description: Record the kept block belongs to, when it belongs to one record.
